{{distinguish|text=the [[Hilbert–Poincaré series]]}} 

In [[number theory]], a '''Poincaré series''' is a [[series (mathematics)|mathematical series]] generalizing the classical [[theta series]] that is associated to any [[discrete group]] of symmetries of a [[complex domain]], possibly of [[several complex variables]].  In particular, they generalize classical [[Eisenstein series]].  They are named after [[Henri Poincaré]].

If &Gamma; is a [[finite group]] acting on a domain ''D'' and ''H''(''z'') is any [[meromorphic function]] on ''D'', then one obtains an [[automorphic function]] by averaging over &Gamma;:
:<math>\sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma} H(\gamma(z)).</math>
However, if &Gamma; is an infinite [[discrete group]], then additional factors must be introduced in order to assure convergence of such a series.  To this end, a '''Poincaré series''' is a series of the form
:<math>\theta_k(z) = \sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma^*} (J_\gamma(z))^k H(\gamma(z))</math>
where ''J''<sub>&gamma;</sub> is the [[Jacobian determinant]] of the group element &gamma;,<ref>Or a more general [[factor of automorphy]] as discussed in {{harvnb|Kollár|1995|loc=§5.2}}.</ref> and the asterisk denotes that the summation takes place only over coset representatives yielding distinct terms in the series.

The classical '''Poincaré series''' of weight 2''k'' of a [[Fuchsian group]] &Gamma; is defined by the series
:<math>\theta_k(z) = \sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma^*} (cz+d)^{-2k}H\left(\frac{az+b}{cz+d}\right)</math>
the summation extending over congruence classes of fractional linear transformations
:<math>\gamma=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}</math>
belonging to &Gamma;.  Choosing ''H'' to be a [[character (group theory)|character]] of the [[cyclic group]] of order ''n'', one obtains the so-called Poincaré series of order ''n'':
:<math>\theta_{k,n}(z) = \sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma^*} (cz+d)^{-2k}\exp\left(2\pi i n\frac{az+b}{cz+d}\right)</math>
The latter Poincaré series converges absolutely and uniformly on compact sets (in the upper halfplane), and is a [[modular form]] of weight 2''k'' for &Gamma;.  Note that, when &Gamma; is the full [[modular group]] and ''n''&nbsp;=&nbsp;0, one obtains the Eisenstein series of weight 2''k''.  In general, the Poincaré series is, for ''n''&nbsp;≥&nbsp;1, a [[cusp form]].
